title: 600-word thread, question buried in the middle
raw: Hey team, wanted to give a full rundown on the Delgado account before our sync tomorrow, sorry in advance for the wall of text, I know this is long but I'd rather over-share than have us walk in without context. We first connected back in March at the regional expo booth, and I remember they seemed genuinely curious about our onboarding flow, though at the time they said budget was locked for the year and there wasn't much point pushing further until the new fiscal year opened up. I followed up in April with a case study from a similar restaurant group, no reply, then again in May with a short video walkthrough of the dashboard, still nothing, not even an out-of-office. June was quiet on my end because I was buried in the Torres renewal, which by the way finally closed after three rounds of legal review, so that's at least one win to report. In July I tried a different angle and sent over our new integrations one-pager since they'd mentioned in passing at the expo that they used a lot of point solutions and were tired of stitching things together manually every month-end. August was mostly internal: we revamped pricing, added a mid-tier plan aimed at exactly this kind of account, and the deck got a full refresh, none of which I actually sent them because I wanted to wait until everything was fully finalized and I didn't want to send something half-baked and then have to correct it later. There was some internal debate about whether Delgado even counts as a real opportunity anymore, since it's been quiet for months now and a couple of people on the team think we should just let it go and reallocate the time elsewhere. Rita thinks we should keep nudging because the account could be sizeable if it ever moves, given the size of their current ops team, but I don't have strong evidence either way beyond a gut feeling and a good first meeting five months ago. Pricing-wise we've gone back and forth internally about whether to lead with the new mid-tier plan or stick to enterprise messaging for this one, and honestly I keep flip-flopping on that depending on the day. Also worth noting, and this might matter more than anything else here: their old champion, the ops director we always spoke with, left the company sometime around June, according to their LinkedIn, so I'm not even sure who the right contact is on their side anymore, but I haven't actually tried to find out who replaced them or whether anyone new has taken over that mandate. There's also a separate thread of internal chatter about whether we should just mark this whole account as stale in the CRM and move on, which I don't fully agree with but I get where it's coming from given how long it's been since anything concrete happened. Anyway, all of that is really just background: the one thing that actually changed this week is that on Monday, out of nowhere, they replied to the July email and just asked: "Can you do a payment plan?" I haven't answered that yet, got pulled into the Q3 close and it slipped through the cracks over the last few days. Let me know if anyone has thoughts before tomorrow's sync, otherwise I'll plan to just answer it myself in the morning. Also a small unrelated reminder while I'm writing all this: Friday is the deadline for expense reports, not related to Delgado at all but I don't want anyone on this thread to miss it since finance has been strict about late submissions this quarter.

caseInput.leadMessages: Can you do a payment plan?
caseInput.notes: Long internal history and pricing debate; their question came in Monday and I haven't answered it yet.
